## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Research notes: will Valencia city suspend in-person classes for weather on Oct 15–16, 2026? (as of 2026-10-05)

All three research angles have now reported, and these notes replace my earlier version. Agents' own probability estimates are left out. Items marked UNVERIFIED have no supporting URL or come from a single search snippet.

## 1. Resolution sources
- **Not read directly:** a fetch of lasprovincias.es was blocked, and nobody fetched the Metaculus FAQ, Levante-EMV or AEMET directly. Everything below comes from other outlets and the city's own site, valencia.es.
- **Nothing published yet for Oct 15–16 (checked 2026-10-05):** no announcement covers those dates.
  - AEMET weather warnings only reach about 3–4 days ahead.
  - Suspensions are usually announced 12–24 hours before, so any decision would most likely come around Oct 13–15.
- **Who decides in Valencia city:** the city council (Ayuntamiento), through its municipal emergency centre (CECOPAL) and the mayor, María José Catalá. The trigger is an AEMET warning or the regional emergency centre's (CCE) alert level.
  - The regional education department (Conselleria d'Educació) does not decide for the city. It only lists the municipalities that suspend.
  - The one exception found is post-damage: after Oct 29, 2024 the Conselleria closed schools in 20 *other* municipalities.
- **Possible ambiguity:** on 2026-10-01 the regional government (Generalitat) declared the red level, but the city's CECOPAL issued the closure order. Earlier city suspensions were all issued by the council.

## 2. The city's suspension protocol
Adopted by the city's civil protection board and published on valencia.es on 2025-09-15: https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/suspensi%C3%B3n-clases-val%C3%A8ncia-alerta-naranja-lluvias

- **AEMET orange rain warning:**
  - Classes are suspended automatically in about 19 centres, if there is enough notice to tell families. These are schools in flood-prone zones and in the outlying districts hit by the 2024 DANA (cut-off low storm).
  - In practice this has grown to 19–31 centres, adding El Saler/Pinedo, El Palmar, Massarrojos, Benimàmet and sometimes the seafront.
  - If the warning arrives while pupils are already in school, the council decides case by case.
- **Red warning:** every school in the city closes (eldiario.es, 2025-09-28): https://www.eldiario.es/comunitat-valenciana/valencia-suspende-clases-zonas-inundables-pedanias-afectadas-dana-naranja-lluvias-alerta_1_12638714.html
- **Relevance:** the question counts a partial suspension. So under this protocol, an orange rain warning for the Valencia coast on Oct 15–16 would very likely produce a qualifying suspension.

## 3. Past suspensions
None of these fall in the question window. They are context for base rates.

- **2019-09-13 (red warning):** all city schools closed. https://www.hortanoticias.com/el-ayuntamiento-de-valencia-suspende-las-clases-en-todos-los-centros-educativos-esta-tarde-y-manana/
- **2024-10-29 (DANA day):** UNVERIFIED whether the city suspended classes. It probably did not.
- **2024-10-30 (red warning):** all city schools closed. https://valenciaplaza.com/ayuntamiento-valencia-suspende-clases-este-miercoles
- **2024-11-13/14:** first the south and seafront, then the whole city. https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/suspensi%C3%B3n-actividad-escolar-1 ; https://www.newtral.es/clases-dana-valencia/20241112/
- **2025-09-29: sources conflict.**
  - One agent reports it started as the 19-school orange suspension and was raised to red, closing every school: https://www.valencia.es/cas/actualidad/-/content/valencia-suspende-actividad-lectiva
  - Another agent describes only the 19-school partial suspension.
- **2025-09-30 (orange):** partial, 31 centres. https://www.elespanol.com/valencia/20250929/colegios-valencia-mantienen-suspension-clases-martes-alerta-naranja/1003743946688_0.html
- **2025-10-13 (orange, DANA Alice):** partial; El Saler and Pinedo were added that afternoon.
  - https://www.eldebate.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/20251012/alerta-naranja-provoca-suspension-clases-algunos-centros-valencia-varios-municipios-este-lunes-13-octubre_343817.html
  - Whether Oct 14–15, 2025 were also suspended is UNVERIFIED.
- **2025-12-15 (orange, Storm Emilia):** partial, about 15 centres. https://www.infobae.com/espana/2025/12/14/valencia-suspende-las-clases-este-lunes-en-varias-pedanias-y-zonas-inundables-ante-la-alerta-naranja-por-lluvias/
- **2026-09-16 (orange):** partial, 26 centres from 14:00. https://www.elperiodicodeaqui.com/valencia/ciudad-de-valencia/estos-son-26-centros-educativos-valencia-suspenden-clases-manana-por-alerta-naranja-lluvias_100120884_102.html
- **2026-10-01/02:** orange partial first, then red, closing all city schools from 15:00 on Oct 1 and all of Oct 2.
  - https://www.eldebate.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/20261001/alerta-roja-lluvias-valencia-ayuntamiento-suspende-clases-todos-centros-educativos-jueves-viernes_464862.html
  - Region-wide, about 356,000 pupils in 103 municipalities had no classes (theobjective.com, 2026-10-01).
  - **The red warning was a near-miss.** The city averaged about 2 L/m² against roughly 180 forecast, and Valencia reportedly asked AEMET to "refine" its forecasts. https://www.eldebate.com/espana/comunidad-valenciana/20261002/alerta-roja-aemet-salda-lluvias-anecdoticas-valencia-apenas-dos-litros-media_465223.html
- **No suspensions found** in Nov 2023 or Mar 2025 (not confirmed either way).

**Rough frequency (agent's count, not a formal base rate):**
- Before the DANA, city suspensions were rare and red-only; 2019 is the only confirmed case.
- Since the protocol (autumn 2025), there have been about 3–4 suspension events per Sep–Dec season.
- Autumn 2026 already has two events: Sep 16 and Oct 1–2.

**Missing data:** no figure was found for how many days per October AEMET puts the Valencia coast on orange or red. AEMET's warnings archive (Meteoalerta) was not checked.

## 4. Calendar and current weather
- **Oct 15 (Thu) and Oct 16 (Fri) 2026 are normal school days.** October's non-school days are Oct 9 and Oct 12.
  - https://comunica.gva.es/es/detalle?id=410987558&site=373430869
  - No local city holiday was found on those dates (not checked against the city's own calendar).
- **2026-10-04/05:** a yellow warning was in force for the northern Valencia coast early on Oct 5, with conditions improving afterwards (eldebate.com, 2026-10-04).
  - It is unconfirmed whether classes resumed normally on Oct 5.
- **AEMET outlook issued 2026-10-02:** for Oct 12–18 it reports "mucha incertidumbre." Rain is possible mainly in the Balearics and the southeast coast. https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/10/02/tiempo-inestable-y-lluvias-en-el-puente-del-12-de-octubre-segun-las-previsiones-de-aemet/
- **Meteored (early October, date uncertain):** a new DANA is forming west-northwest of the Iberian Peninsula, and its final position is uncertain. https://valencianews.es/comunidad-valenciana/prevision-tiempo-valencia-dana-domingo-lunes-martes/
- **Commercial long-range sites** show about 25 °C and partly cloudy skies for Oct 15–18, with a possible storm around Oct 14. These are low-reliability.
- **Sea temperature:** the Mediterranean hit a record 28.54 °C on 2026-08-13 and stayed at or above 28 °C from Aug 5 to Sep 9. https://www.infobae.com/espana/2026/09/06/las-aguas-del-mediterraneo-baten-su-record-historico-de-temperatura-con-maximas-que-superan-los-28-grados/
  - No October figure was found.

## 5. Prediction markets
- **None found:** web searches on 2026-10-05 turned up no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market. The platforms themselves were not searched directly.

criterios: This question resolves YES if the Ayuntamiento de València (Valencia City Council) officially orders the suspension of in-person teaching activity (presential classes) at public and/or private non-university educational centres located within the municipality of Valencia (Spain) for all or part of either October 15 or October 16, 2026, where the stated reason is adverse weather (e.g. an AEMET rainfall/storm warning, DANA, flooding risk, or similar meteorological alert). It resolves NO otherwise. Resolution will be based on official announcements from the Ayuntamiento de València or reporting by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as Las Provincias (https://www.lasprovincias.es/valencia-ciudad/) or Levante-EMV.
letra_pequena: The suspension must apply to the municipality of Valencia itself (the capital city), not merely to other municipalities in the province of Valencia. A suspension affecting even a subset of the city's schools (for example, only centres in flood-prone zones) counts, provided it is ordered by the City Council and the stated motive is adverse weather. Suspensions ordered for reasons unrelated to weather (e.g. strikes, public holidays, scheduled non-teaching days, or structural/building problems) do not count. University closures or shifts to online teaching, on their own, do not count. A suspension order issued before October 15, 2026 that explicitly covers October 15 or 16 counts.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** As of October 5, there are 10–11 days until October 15–16.

(b) **Status quo:** No suspension has been announced for either day; classes are scheduled to take place.

(c) **Reference class:** Since Valencia adopted its precautionary protocol, the city has had roughly 3–4 weather-related suspension episodes per September–December season. That suggests a low-single-digit to roughly 10% chance for a particular two-school-day window, though the sample is small.

(d) **No scenario:** The forecast remains mild, or any rain falls below the warning level that prompts the council to suspend classes.

(e) **Yes scenario:** AEMET issues an orange or red rain warning for October 15 or 16, and the council orders classes suspended in some or all city schools.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** A weather-related council order affecting even a subset of non-university schools **within Valencia city**, or only part of either day, counts. Closures elsewhere in the province do not.

The current forecast does not point clearly to a qualifying storm, so I favor the status quo, while allowing for a warning that emerges closer to the dates.

Probability: 10%

(a) **Time left:** October 15 is 10 days away; the outcome should be known by the end of October 16, about 11 days from now.

(b) **Status quo:** No suspension has been announced for either day, so the outcome is currently NO.

(c) **Reference class:** The research notes identify roughly 3–4 weather-related suspension events during the September–December 2025 school season. That suggests a rough base rate of **around 5–10% for a two-school-day window**, though events are seasonal and can cluster.

(d) **NO scenario:** The forecast remains mild, or any rain alerts stay below the level that prompts a city-ordered suspension.

(e) **YES scenario:** AEMET issues an orange or red rain warning covering Valencia on either day, and the City Council suspends classes under its precautionary protocol.

(f) **Technicality:** A suspension at even a subset of **non-university schools within Valencia city** counts, including one ordered before October 15 that covers either date. Closures only in neighbouring municipalities, or university-only closures, do not.

The recent suspensions and the city’s orange-warning protocol raise the risk above a typical quiet-weather week. But there is no clear severe-weather forecast for October 15–16 yet, so NO remains substantially more likely.

Probability: 10%

(a) **Time left:** The outcome will be known by the end of 16 October 2026, about 11 days away. Any order would most likely be announced around 13–15 October.

(b) **Status quo:** No suspension. Nothing has been announced for 15–16 October. Medium-range forecasts show mild weather with light, occasional rain and no clearly forecast DANA.

(c) **Reference class and base rate:**
- Since the city adopted its orange-warning protocol in autumn 2025, there have been roughly 3–4 weather suspension events per September–December season.
- Each event typically covers 1–2 school days, so about 5–7 suspended days out of roughly 85 school days.
- That gives about a 7–10% chance for any given 2-day window.
- October is the peak torrential-rain month, and autumn 2026 is running wet with a very warm sea. That raises the figure to roughly 10–13% unconditionally.
- Conditioning on the current outlook (mild, no DANA, "mucha incertidumbre" for 12–18 October) brings it down somewhat.

(d) **No scenario:** The week of 12–18 October stays mild with at most yellow warnings, or rain that falls mainly in the Balearics and the southeast. Valencia never reaches an AEMET orange warning for rain on the 15th or 16th, and schools run normally.

(e) **Yes scenario:** The DANA that Meteored says is forming to the west-northwest settles in a favourable position around 14–15 October. AEMET issues an orange warning for the Valencia coast. Under the 2025 protocol, CECOPAL automatically suspends classes at the roughly 19–31 flood-prone and outlying-district schools for the 15th and/or 16th.

(f) **Technicalities:**
- A partial suspension of only the flood-prone schools counts, so an orange warning alone is very likely enough. This is the key factor raising the probability above a red-only base rate.
- The order must come from the City Council. A Generalitat red alert carried out through the city's CECOPAL would still count.
- Suspensions for strikes or holidays do not count. University-only closures do not count.
- An order issued before 15 October counts if it explicitly covers the 15th or 16th.
- The embarrassing near-miss red warning on 1–2 October might make officials slightly more cautious about red-level closures. The orange protocol is automatic, though, so this matters little.

Weighing these, the current forecast pulls the estimate below the October base rate, but real uncertainty remains beyond about 5 days, together with a wet-autumn signal and a low orange-warning trigger.

Probability: 8%
